searches.query: Do entrepreneurial ideas or opportunity insights arise suddenly through incubation and aha moments in the founder's own mind without external input?
kept: Ovington et al. (2015) J Creative Behavior
searches.note: Ovington et al. study when and where aha moments happen (incl. the shower); not entrepreneurs. Consensus (Wiley Scholar Gateway) covers mainly Wiley journals; free query allowance ran out after 6 queries (resets 1 Nov 2026), so later Consensus queries were not run.

searches.query: titles: Gable, Hopper and Schooler (2019); Murphy (2011)
searches.note: Gable et al.: a fifth of the day's most creative ideas came during mind wandering, more often felt as 'aha'. Murphy separates 'eureka' (high serendipity, high deliberation) from 'serendipitous discovery'. Both closed access, abstract only.

searches.query: aha insight opportunity recognition / incubation creativity opportunity idea entrepreneur / eureka moment entrepreneur idea
searches.note: Abstract-only leads: 'Having a creative day' (entrepreneurs' daily idea generation), 'When the muses strike', 'Work hard or play hard: leisure crafting and opportunity recognition', 'Sleep and entrepreneurs' abilities to imagine'.

searches.query: eureka serendipitous discovery legacy deliberate search entrepreneurial discovery 2x2 / single-person single-insight attribution opportunity
searches.note: Vogel's review table lists Murphy's four avenues (serendipitous discovery, eureka, legacy, deliberate search) and Bhave's internal versus external triggers. Dimov (p. 5) notes entrepreneurship's use of Wallas's preparation-incubation-insight stages but argues against single insights; neither calls a purely internal insight serendipity.

searches.query: grep incubat|sudden insight|eureka|aha|dream|external trigger across serendipity papers (Busch 2023, Dew, Yaqub, de Rond, Copeland, Andel, Smith and Hilbolling, Bhave, Oo, Vogel)
searches.note: Busch requires a serendipity trigger (an unplanned event or information) and says apparent spontaneous ideas often rest on forgotten earlier insights; Smith and Hilbolling move away from the eureka-out-of-the-blue image; Andel counts ideas and insights among the elements of a finding and lists dreams among his patterns (already a source of trigger-27). Bhave's 'internally stimulated' recognition is the founder's own need (already background-02). Oo et al. are about how funders perceive serendipity stories.
